one_liner: Linux kernel filesystem on DAX memory with lock-free CAS overlay; authors report up to 2.68x tmpfs random-write throughput.
what_it_does: DAXFS is a GPL-2.0 Linux kernel module plus tools (mkdaxfs, daxfs-inspect) that mounts a filesystem directly on byte-addressable DAX memory: a physical address range, a DAX device or a dma-buf/DMA heap. It targets several kernel instances (multikernel) or, later, CXL-connected hosts sharing one memory region, with a shared namespace, a shared page cache and zero-copy reads. Applications use the normal POSIX file API and mmap; it is a separate mount type, not a tmpfs replacement on block devices, and runs in static (read-only image), split (metadata, overlay and cache in DAX, data in a backing file) or empty (writable, overlay only) modes.
how_it_is_fast: Reads are direct loads from the DAX region with no page-cache copy. Writes go to a copy-on-write hash overlay: an open-addressing, linear-probing table of 16-byte buckets claimed with cmpxchg (FREE to USED), and entries come from a bump allocator advanced with atomic fetch-and-add, so there is no journal, no log and no lock between writers in one coherence domain. A direct-mapped shared page cache with a CAS-driven FREE/PENDING/VALID state machine and clock eviction serves backing-file data to all participants.
when_to_use: Several kernel instances on one cache-coherent machine (multikernel) that must share one read-mostly tree, such as a container base image or LLM model weights, without N copies in memory
Zero-copy CPU or GPU access to file data held in a dma-buf or DMA heap
Concurrent small random writes from several threads to an in-memory filesystem, where the authors measured up to 2.68x tmpfs throughput at 4 threads on DRAM-backed DAX
Research or prototyping on CXL shared-memory filesystems, as a lock-free alternative to famfs's single-master model
when_not_to_use: Block devices or SSDs: the design needs byte-addressable DAX memory and cannot run on block storage
Real multi-host CXL deployments today: the cxl3 backend is a scaffold, and COHERENCE.md says multi-host operation is unsupported until a validation gate passes on CXL 3.0 hardware

Workloads that need strict POSIX write semantics or crash durability: issue #26 reports unserialised i_size updates in daxfs_write_iter() (no inode_lock), #28 says replace-rename is not crash-atomic, and #23 says daxfs_mem_sync() does not flush cache lines

Large or growing writable data sets: the overlay hash table size is fixed at creation, files are capped at about 1M pages (4 GB) by the 20-bit page offset (#22, reported as -ENOSPC), and lookups degrade to a full-table scan once the table fills (#19)
Big-endian machines (#20: CAS loops never terminate) and setups that need device nodes, FIFOs or sockets (no mknod)

integration.form: Linux kernel module (out-of-tree, built with make) plus user-space tools mkdaxfs and daxfs-inspect
integration.dependencies: Linux 5.11+ with CONFIG_FS_DAX; DAX-capable memory (pmem, CXL, DMA heap or dma-buf, or a physical range via /dev/mem)
integration.min_toolchain: Kernel build environment for the target kernel (5.11+); exact compiler not documented
integration.platforms: Linux; coherence primitives described in terms of x86 LOCK CMPXCHG; little-endian only in practice (issue #20)
integration.thread_safety: Lock-free CAS coordination is correct only within one hardware cache-coherence domain (COHERENT backend, default); cross-host CXL3 backend unvalidated; concurrent extending writes race on i_size per issue #26
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: same POSIX file API as tmpfs once mounted, but needs a DAX memory region and mkdaxfs-created image, a fixed-size overlay, and lacks mknod

gotchas: The overlay table and pool are sized at mkdaxfs time (-O, -B); the pool is never compacted, and a full table makes every new page cost a full-table scan (issue #19).
The default mem_model=coherent means one coherence domain; selecting mem_model=cxl3 on ordinary DRAM only exercises plumbing and validates nothing about cross-host coherence.

The performance numbers come from the April 2026 preprint, before May-August 2026 write-path fixes (O_APPEND honoured in the overlay write path, generic_write_checks() and s_maxbytes added), so the measured write path did less checking than the current one.
Mounting an image from untrusted sources should use the validate mount option; issue #21 reports daxfs_mem_ptr() bounds-checks only the start offset of a read span.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick DAXFS over NOVA, WineFS or SplitFS when the need is sharing one in-memory filesystem across kernel instances or a dma-buf with lock-free concurrent writers, rather than durable persistent-memory storage for a single kernel; MadFS and SplitFS are user-space PM file systems for one host and do not offer a shared namespace.
verified_claims_summary: The authors' arXiv preprint 2604.01620 (seen only through search-result snippets; arxiv.org and alphaxiv are egress-blocked) reports that on single-host DRAM-backed DAX DaxFS beats tmpfs on all write workloads, up to 2.68x random-write throughput at 4 threads, and 1.18x random-read throughput at 64 KB; hardware, kernel, compiler and fio parameters were not visible. The same snippet describes cross-host validation only under QEMU-emulated CXL 3.0, with '>99% CAS accuracy', a wording that does not obviously match its 'no lost updates' claim.
status_note: Active but single-maintainer (all recent commits by congwang-mk, last 2026-08-16), 102 stars, 11 open issues including six labelled bugs; GPL-2.0 kernel code is copyable but needs a kernel build and a DAX setup.
sources_read: WebSearch: DAXFS lock-free shared filesystem CXL disaggregated memory arXiv 2604.01620 (snippet of https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.01620)
